verdict: The spine is strong exactly where Indonesian is unlike Hindi – the zero copula, the you-ladder, sudah/belum, the aspect words, -nya, yang, and the sambal/warung/ojek layer – and the register instinct (bikin, ngomong, banget, aja, soalnya) is right for the brief. Three things undercut it. First, roughly 200 items are straight duplicates of earlier items at contradictory tiers (ojek x3, sambal x3, yang x3, mas/mbak x4, plus pakai, ayam, tempe, tahu, nasi goreng, mie goreng, gorengan, nasi campur, santan, macet, HP, sinyal, salim, Lebaran, tante, om, -nya, kan, vegetarian), so the effective syllabus is nearer 950 teachables than 1,154 and the tier signal is unreliable wherever a word appears twice. Second, the Hindi frame left real holes a learner walks into on day one: bayar is absent entirely, as is nggak as a headword, the '…, nggak?' yes/no question pattern that the deck's own example sentences silently depend on, any pronunciation guidance for a roman-script language full of traps (c = ch, schwa e, swallowed final k), the whole accommodation exchange (ada kamar kosong / boleh lihat kamarnya / termasuk sarapan), getting lost, calling the police, renting a scooter, halal, pantai, dompet, sebelah, jemput, Selamat jalan, Selamat datang, Salam kenal, and the me-/ber- recognition rule needed to read a single sign – while thirteen slots go to mertua and ipar compounds that Indonesian collapses into two words. Third, a handful of items are wrong rather than merely misplaced: bikin is glossed 'to do' (that's ngapain), hs-0462 explains the tahu/tahu pair as vowel length when it is h-retention versus contraction, hs-0958 reverses banget and sekali, 'Senang bertemu dengan Anda' uses the very pronoun hs-0005 warns against, and 'Tolong pelan-pelan' to a driver means slow down rather than speak slowly. Two tier-6 N/A calls are also wrong in kind – yogurt and 'happy birthday' both exist in Indonesian and are simply low-value, which is a tier-5 fact, not a gap. One flag for the parent before any of this is authored: docs/indonesian-register-policy.md in this repo classes nggak, banget and udah as register offenders below Q4, which is in direct conflict with a syllabus that teaches them as tier-1 production; that has to be resolved first or the register gate will reject the deck it produces.
